claim_verdicts.evidence: OrdersController.cs @stage-1 lines 19-28: method body has no `if`/`switch`; the only `return` is `return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order));` (line 27). Preceding lines only build `customerId`, `items`, `order`.

RFC 9110 §9.3.3: "If one or more resources has been created on the origin server as a result of successfully processing a POST request, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field that provides an identifier for the primary resource created (Section 10.2.2) and a representation that describes the status of the request while referring to the new resource(s)." Verbatim in local mirror.

RFC 9110 §9.2.2: "A request method is considered 'idempotent' if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request. Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent." POST is absent from that list.

Dtos.cs @stage-1 line 13: `public sealed record CreateOrderRequest(List<CreateOrderItemRequest> Items);` — one positional parameter, no id. `CreateOrderItemRequest` (line 11) is `(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd)`, also no id.

ASP.NET Core docs on CreatedAtAction: "Adds a Location header to the response. The Location header specifies the URI of the newly created to-do item." and "References the `GetTodoItem` action to create the `Location` header's URI." Execution confirms the route source: OrdersController.Get is `[HttpGet("{id:int}")]` under `[Route("api/v1/orders")]`, and the live POST returned `Location: http://localhost:8080/api/v1/orders/15`.

Live run against the stage-1 lab: POST /api/v1/orders with a valid JSON body and NO Authorization header returned `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`, `Content-Length: 0` — the body never ran. Source line 21 reads the identity, not the body: `var customerId = int.Parse(User.FindFirstValue(JwtRegisteredClaimNames.Sub)!);`, and CreateOrderRequest has no customer field.

claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Live run: sending the identical POST /api/v1/orders request (same token, same body) twice in a row created two separate orders with two different ids, both answered 201, neither reusing or rejecting the other's id (observed ids differ per run).

issues.text: Unlisted claim: the lesson defines `200` as meaning the answer pre-existed. RFC 9110 §15.3.1 says only "The 200 (OK) status code indicates that the request has succeeded", and Table 6 gives POST's 200 content as "the status of, or results obtained from, the action" — i.e. 200 is routinely used for POSTs that change state. The claim is not in the ledger, and it is reused in section 9 line 1 and in quiz q6's explanation for option c ("`200` claims the answer already existed").
issues.quote: `200` means the request succeeded and the answer already existed
issues.fix: Rewrite as a statement about what 201 adds, not about what 200 asserts: "`200` says only that the request succeeded; `201` says that and adds that the request created a new resource." Apply the same correction to five-line summary line 1 and to quiz q6's explanation for option c (say `200` loses information the client needs, not that it "claims the answer already existed").

issues.text: Unconditional wording contradicts the ledger's own claim 2 (which correctly says SHOULD) and RFC 9110 §15.3.2: "The primary resource created by the request is identified by either a Location header field in the response or, if no Location header field is received, by the target URI." A 201 without Location is legal. Repeated verbatim as five-line summary line 2.
issues.quote: a `201` response carries a `Location` header naming the new resource's own URL
issues.fix: Add the condition: "a `201` for a newly created resource should carry a `Location` header naming that resource's own URL — the Đơn Hàng API always sends one —". Update five-line summary line 2 the same way ("A `201` from `POST /api/v1/orders` carries a `Location` header…").
